newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Guerrilla in Israeli embassy blast on hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Guerrilla in Israeli embassy blast on hunger strike.

text.p: A Palestinian jailed in Cyprus for a bungled car bomb attack against the Israeli embassy in 1988 has gone on a hunger strike because he cannot find a country willing to accept him now he is free, a Cypriot newspaper reported on Thursday.
"I will not take food unless something is done," Omar Hawillo, 36, told the mass-circulation daily Philelephtheros, which carried the report on Thursday.
"I am ready to die rather than stay in prison," he added.
Police confirmed he has been on a hunger strike for a week.

Hawillo, initially from Lebanon, was jailed for 15 years in 1988 for his part in a bomb explosion close to the embassy of Israel in the capital Nicosia, which killed three people and injured 19. He pleaded guilty to two manslaughter charges.
A jeep rigged with explosives went off on a bridge after security personnel twice prevented the driver from parking outside the Israeli embassy building.
Two Cypriot passers-by and the Lebanese driver of the jeep, Hawillo's suspected accomplice, were killed.
Hawillo was released from prison last year. Ten months later, he is without travel documents and still in detention at a police station, not finding any country willing to accept him.
It was never clarified to which militant faction Hawillo belonged.
"He is like a spent cartridge," an Arab diplomatic source told Reuters. "There isn't one country in the region that will accept him because of his background."
Hawillo is not eligible for help from the United Nations refugee agency, the UNHCR, either.
"His case was sent for review in Geneva and it was decided he does not qualify as a refugee," Michael Menning, head of the Cyprus mission, told Reuters.
"What we did do as a good offices mission is let embassies know of the situation and pursue it, if they wish to. There is nothing else we can do," he said.
